item.itunes:summary:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g8OfzDJuy4s

值得閱讀的理由

  • 破除 AI 術語焦慮：提供一套清晰實用的「三層判斷法則」，幫助讀者在面對層出不窮的新詞時，精準判斷該忽略、微調還是重構工作流。
  • 洞悉底層本質：深入拆解 Context Engineering 與 Prompt Engineering 的關係，說明為何「清晰表達意圖」的能力永不過時。
  • 掌握 Agent 關鍵架構：解析 Graph Engineering 與 Agent Harness 的工程核心，掌握多代理協同的解耦原則與運行環境支撐機制。

摘要

破除名詞焦慮：面對 AI 新概念的三種判斷準則

面對如雨後春筍般湧現的 AI 新名詞，業界常充斥著「舊方法已過時、必須重新學習」的焦慮。作者指出，使用者並不需要每次都打掉重練，而是應該依據三種情境採取不同行動：第一種是「舊問題、舊方法」的換皮包裝，只需保持認知即可；第二種是「核心任務不變但複雜度與失敗路徑增加」（如單輪對話演變為長鏈條流程），此時僅需吸收一至兩個核心原則並微調習慣；第三種則是「任務邊界與人工操作發生根本性改變」，唯有此時才真正需要重構整體工作流程。

上下文工程與提示工程的本質思辨

針對近期熱門的 Context Engineering（上下文工程），作者認為所有給 AI 的輸入本質上都是 Prompt，組織輸入本就是 Prompt Engineering（提示工程）一直以來的核心。雖然在 Agent 時代長執行鏈中，動態資料檢索與狀態維護的複雜度確實增加，但這屬於系統複雜度提升，而非變成一門全新學科。使用者只需掌握「在長流程中清理無效上下文」以及「關鍵節點記錄狀態」等原則即可。作者強調，除非未來 AI 能像外星文明般直接心靈感應（讀心），否則人類清晰向機器表達意圖的能力永遠不會過時。

圖工程架構思維：解耦執行與人工驗證

在探討多代理協同的 Graph Engineering（圖工程）時，作者指出 Agent 絕非越多越好，而是需要能真正提升品質的最小可行集合。構建 Agent 架構時有兩大關鍵原則：首先是必須將「執行任務」與「檢查評分」的責任完全解耦分離；其次是在可能產生高昂錯誤成本的關鍵節點，必須引入「人工驗證」。作者認為這並非憑空誕生的魔法，而是建立在經典軟體工程與系統設計的基礎上，使用者無須恐慌報班，只需將嚴格驗收的思維落實到交付階段。

Agent Harness：大模型背後的運行支撐系統

最後，作者解析了備受矚目的 Agent Harness（代理運行架構）。Harness 本質上是環繞在大模型周圍的運行環境與支撐系統，負責連接外部工具、維護執行狀態及校驗結果。其技術核心在於「一切皆插件」的模組化設計，並透過可追溯的日誌支持狀態復原與分支重試，能極大化釋放大模型潛能。同時，作者也提醒需保持動態平衡：隨著底層大模型能力快速增強，原本繁瑣外置的人工干預規則應適時剔除，避免過度設計。

================================================

# 新词又刷屏：Agent = Model + Harness

DeepSeek recently released the. developer preview of Hness, with an. official page featuring a direct. formula: agent equals model plus. Just. a while ago, everyone was talking about. context engineering and graph. engineering—how long has it really. been? Now, H is everywhere. Every time. a new buzzword drops, the internet is. flooded with voices claiming your old. methods are obsolete and you need to. relearn everything. With AI terms. constantly rotating, do you really. intend to relearn everything every. single time? In today’s episode, we. won’t be discussing product features; instead, I’ll give you three. actionable judgment moves you can use. immediately. When the next buzzword. emerges, do you really just need to be. aware of it, is it worth absorbing a. couple of key principles, or do you. truly need to overhaul your entire. workflow? Hey there, hello, and welcome. back. Every time a new term pops up,. everyone is actually struggling with. the same thing. On one hand, you’re. genuinely afraid of missing out on. major underlying changes and falling. behind; on the other hand, you really. don't want to spend every weekend glued. to your computer relearning the same. old concepts repackaged as something. new. So, let’s use this opportunity. to clear up this confusion once and for. all. Whenever a new AI term appears in. the industry, you actually only have.

# 三种情况，三个动作

three choices. The first scenario: old. problem, old methods. The core problem. to be solved remains the same, and the. solution method is identical; it’s. purely just a new term used for. repackaging. When facing these terms,. your action is simple: just be aware of. it. Understand what your peers are. talking about, and that's it—no need. to spend tons of energy learning it in. depth. As for the second scenario, the. problem itself hasn't changed, but the. complexity and the ways it can fail. have. The core task remains the same,. but...The scenario might have shifted. from a single turn of conversation to a. long, complex process chain, and the. points of failure might be completely. different. In this case, your action is. to absorb one or two principles; there’s no need to completely. overthrow or abandon your existing. system—just tweaking your habits to. address the new issues is enough. In. the third scenario, the boundaries of. the task and the specific manual. actions you take every day have. fundamentally changed. The things the. system can take over have changed, and. the sequence of your workflow, your. final deliverables, and the way you. verify quality have all changed as well. . Only when facing these types of terms. does it really become time for our. third action: modifying our workflow. However, just laying out these three. categories isn't very useful; the key. is how we determine which type a newly. emerged buzzword actually belongs to. Next, let's take Context Engineering,. Graph Engineering, and RAG Harness as. examples and go through them one by one.

# Context Engineering 归哪一类

. Let's start with the first term,. Context Engineering, which has been. incredibly popular lately. Many people. feel that Prompt Engineering is. completely obsolete, and everyone is. discussing how to learn Context. Engineering from scratch. Actually, as. early as October 20, 2023, I posted a. public tweet on X where my point was. very clear: aren't all inputs to AI. essentially prompts? How to organize. inputs to be more effective for the. model is exactly what Prompt. Engineering has been doing all along. Context is inherently the core. component of prompt engineering; there. is absolutely no need to package it as. an independent new term. Is this term. just a case of making things up out of. thin air? Well, not exactly. Since. entering the Agent era, systems often. need to dynamically retrieve external. data. In long execution chains, context. is easily lost or corrupted, and we. also need to manage intermediate states. , ensuring we can recover whenever. errors occur. So, the complexity and. potential for errors have indeed. genuinely increased, but separating it. out doesn't mean it has become an. independent discipline. The market. loves to take upgrades in system. complexity and hype them up as entirely. new, independent disciplines. If you. treat it as a brand-new field to study,. you'll subconsciously feel that your. previous logic and knowledge are. obsolete, falling once again into. endless learning anxiety. In fact, what. you should do right now is just absorb. a couple of key principles. For. instance, in long processes, pay. attention to clearing out ineffective. context and leaving records of your. state at critical nodes. Integrating. these one or two principles into your. usual workflow is enough to handle. these changes; there's no need to. overturn everything you already know.

Why was I so confident in making that.

# 我为什么敢这么笃定

judgment back then? Because it's easy. to judge; it definitely wasn't. something I just threw together for. today's video. We can look back at the. timeline; as early as July 25, 2023, I. made a video discussing the three major. starting points of AI. Back then in. that video, I said that until AI can. read minds, prompt engineering won't. become obsolete. In 2020, I reaffirmed. this: only when AI can truly read minds. , and humans no longer need language to. communicate with it, will the act of. expressing our intent lose its meaning.

The specific techniques will certainly. change, but the ability to clearly. articulate intent will never be. outdated. As of February 10, 2026, I. wrote in a tweet again that AI will. only render prompt engineering. meaningless in one scenario: when it. can read our minds like the Trisolarans. . Looking back from 2023, 2024, all the. way to 2026, over these three years,. almost every time a new technology or. concept emerged, there would be a. chorus of voices online declaring that. old skills were being phased out. But. the underlying logic is actually very. simple: as long as machines still. require humans to explain their intent,. the core of this skill remains. unchanged. While the buzzwords on the. surface have been swapped out time and. again, this underlying principle has. consistently held true. Now, let's look.

# Graph Engineering 与那两条原则

at another term that has been. frequently discussed recently: Graph. Engineering. When people began using AI. to run complex tasks, concepts like. multi-agent orchestration and. topological network structures. immediately became hot topics. When. discussing agent architecture, creator. Greg Assenberg mentioned several very. practical principles: agents are. definitely not the more the better; we. need the minimum viable set that can. truly improve quality. Those. responsible for execution and those. responsible for checking and scoring. must be completely separated, and at. critical nodes where errors could lead. to high costs, human verification is. mandatory. These principles might sound. like entirely new concepts, but if you. have watched my previous videos, you. would find they align perfectly with my. own logic. I previously talked. specifically about why you should never. blindly trust an AI when it reports. that it has finished a task, and why. you must return to the actual generated.

documents to verify them with your own. eyes. If you look at these two things. together, they sit at two different. stages: his focus is on how to. reasonably divide labor at the system. architecture level, while mine is on. how to strictly gatekeep the delivery. and acceptance phase. Of course, I'm. not saying all new concepts are just. marketing; some of these new ideas do. correspond to real capabilities and. represent a genuine step forward. We've. moved from simple Q&A to stateful. interactions, capable of pausing and. resuming at any time, invoking various. tools, and handling long-running. processes that require human. confirmation at critical steps; this. change is real. However, the term " agent" is still built on the classic. foundations of software engineering and. system design, so there's no need to. panic and sign up for a new course; the. core remains absorbing those two key. principles: decouple execution from. verification, and perform manual. sign-offs at critical nodes. Now, let's.

return to the focus of the beginning:.

# DeepSeek Harness 到底是什么

the agent harness. Why are both major. vendors and individual developers all. moving toward the direction of. harnesses now? The official. documentation for the agent framework. makes it very clear in the developer. preview. Everything is a plugin.

Everything is a plugin: models, tools,. skills, planning, management,. sandboxing, storage, and schedulers—. all these modules are designed to be. plug-and-play. Furthermore, by. maintaining a complete, append-only. history of execution logs, the system. supports real-time backtracking,. tracing, state recovery, and even. branching off to try a different path.

In terms of engineering, the OpenAI. team revealed that they generated about. a million lines of code in just five. months. On average, each engineer. merged 3.5 pull requests per day, and. not a single line of the entire project. was typed by a human; this set of. numbers is a staggering reference for. how much an external runtime. environment and an agent harness can. amplify a large model's capabilities. So, what exactly is an agent harness? To put it simply, it is the runtime. environment and support system. surrounding the large model,. specifically responsible for. interfacing with external tools,. maintaining execution state, and. performing result validation. In their. engineering article on long-running. tasks, OpenAI mentioned a very. insightful observation: many. assumptions and intervention rules. carefully designed in the early stages. of an agent will quickly become. obsolete as the model's own. capabilities improve; external steps. that the model can handle itself should. be firmly removed. Therefore, the core. lies in striking the right balance; it. is absolutely not the case that a. thicker, more complex framework with. more rules is necessarily more advanced. . You must constantly prune the steps. the model can handle itself, but. fundamental system responsibilities—. such as how to persist state, how to. isolate permissions, how to resume. after an interruption, and who. validates the results—must, in any. case, be carried by someone or another. system. So, when does a new term truly.

# 什么时候才真要改工作流

require you to overhaul your entire. workflow? The key is whether your task. boundaries and the specific actions you. perform every day have truly undergone. a fundamental change. Take my usual. content production workflow: I used to. write scripts by chatting with AI from. start to finish in a single window, but. now, the whole process is broken down. into several independent stages, with. standard files used for handoffs. between steps, and key points must be. manually confirmed. A simple example:. for the script of the video you're. watching now, the first time I ran the. entire automated process, it hit a. pending issue at the final validation. stage and just stopped right there,. refusing to produce any output at all.

It didn't just deliver a "good enough" rough draft for me to adjust myself. It. flatly refused to deliver anything. until I resolved every issue it flagged. and re-ran the process, only then did I. get the usable draft you see now. You. see, this is what that third scenario. actually looks like. It’s not about. me learning another trendy buzzword; it’s about the sequence of my daily. tasks, the way I hand off work between. tools, and when I am forced to stop—. that is what truly changes my work. OK,. while we're on this topic, I need to. confess something to you all. I have. created concepts in the past, such as.

# 我也造过概念：MAPS

the MAPS framework I proposed. However,. the logic I followed in naming it is. exactly what we're discussing today; it. was never about dressing up old. concepts in trendy clothes, but because. it is based on a verified, stable. structure. The letters in MAPS stand. for Mindset, Architecture, Prompting,. and System—the four traits I believe. a super-individual must possess in the. AI era. When I wrote my book " Reconstructing the Individual," these. four layers were its backbone. You can. see that even though tools and models. have changed over the years, the. underlying logic of these four layers. has never shifted. I propose this. framework to help you see clearly which. layer you are currently stuck on at any. given moment. It’s to show you where. to focus your efforts next, not to. create a new set of homework for you to. memorize. So, my goal today is not to. stand on a moral high ground and. condescendingly oppose creating new. terms; in a commercial society, coining. new terms is simply an objective law of. market communication. What we really. need to watch out for is that bandwagon. mentality—where you don't do any. thinking or judgment of your own, but. just frantically grab whatever. buzzwords others throw your way. When. it comes to the endless stream of new. terms, you only need to remember this. one sentence: Stop chasing tools, start. building leverage. Don't just keep. chasing new tools; save your energy to. build the kind of long-term leverage. that truly belongs to you. If you're. looking to build more than just the. ability to judge a single new term, but. rather a systematic way of thinking. that you can use in the long run, the. link to the MAPS Thinking Compass is in. the pinned comment and description box. Feel free to check it out whenever you. like. y.

DeepSeek 放出 Harness 的开发者预览，官方页面直接写了个公式：Agent = Model + Harness。前阵子还在聊 Context Engineering、Graph Engineering，这才多久，Harness 又刷屏了。每冒出一个新词，总有一堆声音说你原来那套已经过时了。

这期不讲产品功能，只给你三个拿来就能用的判断动作：这个新词你是只需要知道即可，还是值得吸收一两条原则，还是真的必须去大改工作流。

本期用三个真实的词逐个拆解：

✅ Context Engineering：复杂度变了，但不等于它变成了一门独立学科

✅ Graph Engineering：底层依然是经典软件工程的老常识，吸收两条原则就够

✅ DeepSeek Harness：万物皆插件，以及框架不是搭得越厚越先进

我也把自己 2023 年 7 月到 2026 年 2 月的三次公开记录摆出来，看看这三年外面的词换了多少茬，底层判断动过没有。

🎯 适合人群：

• 每次新词刷屏就担心自己落后的 AI 学习者

• 不想每个周末都从头再学一遍的知识工作者

• 想要一套判断标准，而不是又一份工具清单的创作者
